diff: +77 LAFAN1 motions — 496,672 frames — onto Unitree G1
+Higher is faster. Click the chart to view it full size.
+Lower is faster. Parallel values are aggregate wall time per frame.
+). Even this slowest tested FRDV 2.0 configuration exceeds every competing setup tested, including their fastest 8-worker/device runs. Its throughput is
+that of the fastest competing result, FRAX with 8 CPU devices, in this warm LAFAN1 benchmark.

+one warm pass over all 77 LAFAN1 motions on an Apple M1 (8 CPU cores, 8 GiB RAM), using the official GMR and FRAX code. Processing includes loading, target preparation, kinematic retargeting, and enabled cleanup; shared startup, compilation, and saving are excluded. FPS is total original frames divided by elapsed processing time; µs/frame is its reciprocal, not isolated single-frame latency. Configurations run separately; each pipeline retains its configured tasks and constraints. The FRDV 1.0 comparison uses its fastest measured variant: an external 8-file-worker pool without chunking or boundary refinement. These are single-run throughput measurements, not a comparison of identical tracking objectives or motion quality.
+FRDV 2.0 keeps constrained per-frame SQP, temporal warm starts, and robot joint limits. The execution path is rebuilt around the small, repeated problems that motion retargeting actually solves.

+Forward kinematics, Jacobians, Gauss–Newton QP construction, line search, and the frame loop run inside one compiled whole-clip call. Preallocated workspaces reuse memory across frames, avoiding repeated Python calls and temporary allocations.

+A dense Goldfarb–Idnani active-set solver replaces the previous general-purpose OSQP path. It reuses the active constraint set between neighboring frames, matching the small, closely related QPs encountered along a motion.

+Native calls release Python’s GIL, so threads solve different files concurrently with a workspace per worker. Each clip keeps its temporal history: no default within-clip chunking, process-to-process trajectory copying, or chunk-boundary stitching. Enabled despike cleanup stays in the measured pipeline.
+You are now viewing the original FRDV paper & research results.
